title: No-Show Follow-Up Automation: How to Set It Up (2026)
summary: No show follow up automation workflows ensure missed appointments are converted into rescheduled meetings through triggered email or SMS sequences.
body_markdown:
## How to automate no-show follow-up sequences


### The anatomy of an automated recovery workflow


An effective recovery flow operates as a persistent listener that only acts when specific conditions are met. It begins with a trigger from a scheduling tool like[Calendly](https://calendly.com/pricing) or a calendar provider like Microsoft Outlook.


Rather than firing immediately, the system initiates a "Wait" step to allow for the meeting duration to pass.


Once the time is up, the system queries the meeting platform (such as Zoom or Google Meet) to check if the participant's "Joined" timestamp is null.


If the system confirms the attendee is absent, the flow branches: it updates the lead status in a CRM like HubSpot and dispatches a "Sorry we missed you" message via an email provider like Gmail or an SMS service like Twilio.


Every other platform searches its templates. Activepieces writes yours.


Describe the recovery logic to the built-in AI chat (for example, "when a Cal.com event ends with no attendee, wait 15 minutes then update HubSpot and text the lead via Twilio") and it constructs and publishes that specific flow even if no template exists for it, effectively automating complex workflows without requiring pre-built integrations, which means users can deploy custom automations instantly without needing technical expertise.


### Why manual follow-ups fail in 2026


Manual follow-ups rely on the host’s memory and immediate availability, which creates a bottleneck when back-to-back meetings occur.


If a Sales Development Representative has five calls in a row and the second one is a no-show, they often lack the window to stop, open their CRM, and draft a manual email before the next call begins.


By the time the workday ends, the context of the missed meeting has faded. This delay signals to the prospect that their time and the potential partnership aren't priorities for the company.


### The 'golden hour' for rebooking missed meetings


The likelihood of re-engaging a lead drops significantly as time passes. Data comparing recovery methods shows that automated sequences capture more missed opportunities than manual efforts within the first two days of a ghosted call.


> The likelihood of re-engaging a lead drops significantly as time passes.


**60% recovery rates** are reached because automation hits the inbox while the prospect is likely still at their desk, feeling the slight guilt of a missed commitment.


Following this immediate outreach, the workflow can then schedule a secondary task for the account owner if no rebooking occurs within the next day.
